answer: A lagoon stays clear when its inlet is guarded and every boat is logged; a smuggler loses cargo and pass. Copy that rule: each identity locks a deposit and waits through rate-limited onboarding, one identity per deposit, no bulk creation. Like saffron, precious because each flower yields little, an identity must spend time and funds before full rights, while quartz is common but a cut gem is not: the system watches behavior fingerprints, and identities in lockstep forfeit deposits. A Sybil farmer can mint clones, but each costs a bond plus a wait, so forging thousands stops being cheap.
